records.quote: Lemma 1 (Lemma 3.1 of Xu and Balakrishnan (2012)). Let F be a distribution function with density f supported on (0, ∞) such that f(e^x) is log concave in x ∈ R. Let G1, . . . , Gn be distribution functions with densities g1, . . . , gn supported on (0, ∞) such that F ≤* Gi for each i = 1, . . . , n. Then F ≤* Σ_{i=1}^n pi Gi for pi > 0 such that Σ_{i=1}^n pi = 1.
records.family: arbitrary distributions on (0, ∞) with log-concave-in-exponential-scale density for F
records.compared: F vs mixture of Gi, each star-larger than F

conclusion.direction: F <=_* Σ pi Gi (mixture preserves star ordering)

records.quote: Lemma 4 (Theorem 1 of Yu (2016)). Suppose α ≥ 1. Suppose 0 < θ1 ≤ · · · ≤ θn and η1 ≤ · · · ≤ ηn and (a) there exists 2 ≤ k ≤ n such that θi < ηi for i < k and θi > ηi for i ≥ k; (b) Π ηi > Π θi. Then there exists x0 ∈ (0, ∞) such that Fη(x) < Fθ(x) for x ∈ (0, x0) and the inequality is reversed for x > x0.

records.claim: Restated result of Bon & Pǎltǎnea (2006) [Introduction, eq. (1)]
records.quote: Let X1,...,Xn be independent exponential random variables with rates λ1,...,λn respectively. Let Y1,...,Yn be another set of independent exponential random variables with a common rate γ. Then the kth order statistic of the heterogeneous sample is larger than that of the homogeneous sample in the usual stochastic order, that is, Yk:n ≤st Xk:n, if and only if γ ≥ ( C(n,k)^{-1} sk(λ1,...,λn) )^{1/k} [γ ≥ (sk(λ1,...,λn)/ inom{n}{k})^{1/k}], where sk denotes the kth elementary symmetric function.
records.family: Independent exponential samples: heterogeneous rates λi (X) vs homogeneous rate γ (Y)

hypotheses.text: Xi ~ exponential(λi) independent; Yi ~ exponential(γ) iid

records.ambiguity: Background result quoted; related restated facts: k = n case implies hazard rate and dispersive orders (Khaledi & Kochar 2000), k = 2 equivalence with ≤hr (Pǎltǎnea 2008).
